text:
maria.g: Heads-up: customer acme-inc reported a sharp p95/p99 regression on /v1/generate starting ~2026-03-14T00:50Z. p50 same, p95 jumped from ~320ms to 1.8s and p99 to ~3.6s. Affects hosted-GPU pool in us-west-2. Visible in their support ticket #4521. I can share logs and request IDs on demand.
raj.s: thanks. any recent infra changes around 00:30-01:00? kernel/driver/firmware deployments?
maria.g: ops change log shows a GPU driver rollout (535.xx) started at 00:47 across the hosted pool. Also a host-kernel patch rolled to a subset of nodes at 00:40. Not sure of overlap yet.
oliver.k: I’m seeing increased per-request latency spikes correlated with NVMe io wait on the affected nodes. KV-cache hit ratio dropped ~18% for that model, likely due to higher eviction/serialization delays.
ingrid.s: can we get iostat/blktrace + nvidia metrics from an affected host? tag one host id and I’ll pull traces.
maria.g: tagged host gpu-host-ww-12-3. Logs uploaded to /shared/incidents/4521/ (link: https://vault/redwood/incidents/4521). Quick paste of iostat output from 00:45-01:15:

```
Device:         rrqm/s   wrqm/s     r/s     w/s    rkB/s    wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz   await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1           0.00    20.00  120.00  300.00  51200.00  102400.00  512.00   6.70   14.2   3.1    18.4   0.90  36.00
```

avgqu-sz jumped 6x vs baseline.
raj.s: that aligns with storage IO contention. But why would that cause p99 spikes for inference? plausible chain: driver update changes DMA behavior or pinned memory churn -> causes more synchronous NVMe flushes? We need perf counters.
oliver.k: on the runtime side, when NVMe stalls, KV-cache fetches timeout and we fall back to disk and to model recompute; that kills tail latency. Also batching windows lengthen under backpressure.
danielle.p: I can reproduce locally against a staging cluster if you give me a repro load. What payload / concurrency did customer use?
maria.g: they reported steady concurrency ~18 with sequence length ~512, tokens out ~350. Using model redwood-llama-13b-rev1 via hosted route /v1/chat/completions.

--- Repro steps (for SRE/eng):
1) curl load test (concurrency 18):
```
ab -n 1000 -c 18 -p small_payload.json -T application/json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
```
or better: wrk2 script hitting the endpoint with JSON bodies at fixed throughput.
2) collect these on the target node:
```
sudo iostat -x 1 > /tmp/iostat.out &
sudo blktrace -d /dev/nvme0n1 -o - | blkparse -i - > /tmp/blktrace.out &
nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 > /tmp/gpu_dmon.out &
```
3) on the inference process (pid):
```
sudo perf record -F 99 -p <pid> -g -- sleep 60
sudo perf script > /tmp/perf.unfold
```

raj.s: good. collect also kernel trace (perf/tracepoints) for nvme completion latency and DMA stats. We want to see whether driver 535 introduced different queue depths or polling behaviour.
maria.g: I've already got dmesg snippets showing many `nvme: I/O submission timeout` warnings on that host starting 00:48. Dropping paste:

```
[00:48:12] nvme nvme0: I/O submission timeout, resetting controller
[00:48:12] nvme nvme0: failed abort; error -110
[00:48:14] nvme nvme0: controller reset done.
```

oliver.k: wow, controller resets will absolutely spike latency. That could be firmware-host driver mismatch. Which node images got the firmware upgrade? Ingrid?
ingrid.s: firmware rollout was scheduled but only a small set applied; however the driver rollout touched all nodes. Hypothesis: new driver + older NVMe firmware causes recovery loops under high load.
danielle.p: reproduce plan: pick a node from the affected pool, simulate concurrency 18 with seq 512 -> confirm I/O resets and p99 spikes. If confirmed, we can mitigate by routing traffic off the affected nodes and rolling back driver on the pool.

--- Immediate mitigations (proposal):
maria.g: 1) Add a node taint on affected nodes so the scheduler won't place new inference pods there: kubectl taint nodes gpu-host-ww-12-3 redwood=degraded:NoSchedule
raj.s: 2) Update routing policy to avoid those host IDs in hosted pool for 30m (we can mark hosts unhealthy in control plane).
oliver.k: 3) Temporary increase replica count in unaffected pool to absorb traffic and set autoscaler to be more aggressive.
ingrid.s: 4) Rollback GPU driver package for the affected shard of hosts to previous known-good (525.x) — need change approval. That should stop the controller resets if our hypothesis is correct.
danielle.p: 5) As a short-term customer-facing mitigation, enable model-fallback: direct affected customers to model-variant with lower memory pressure (quantized variant) to reduce KV cache churn.

maria.g: I initiated a routing change to mark gpu-host-ww-12-* as degraded. Support message to acme-inc: we suspect infra regression, routing traffic to healthier pool and continuing investigation. Customer acknowledged and accepted temporary routing.

--- Investigation notes / telemetry we collected:
- KV cache hit ratio dashboard: sharp drop starting 00:50.
- NVMe controller reset logs on 7 hosts in the hosted pool between 00:47-00:59.
- iostat showing avgqu-sz & await increases; %util for nvme0n1 > 85%.
- Kernel logs include `nvme: aborting command` messages.
- Driver rollout records show version bumped to 535.86 across hosted at 00:47; previous stable was 525.85.

raj.s: next steps: if rollback proves safe, schedule rollback for affected nodes during low traffic with canary verify on two nodes. If rollback delayed, temporary capacity shift + firmware vendor check.

ingrid.s: I'll engage storage vendor and NVMe firmware team to check for known issues with driver 535.x and controller family X. Also opening support ticket with cloud provider.

oliver.k: after rollback, we should run stress test with seq 1024, concurrency 24 to exercise worst-case and ensure no submission timeouts.

sre-bot: INCIDENT-4521 created, severity elevated to SEV-2. Pager duty rotation: raj.s -> oncall.

support-bot: Notifying customer acme-inc: "We've routed your traffic to healthy hosts and are actively investigating. We'll follow up in 30 min with telemetry and ETA for rollback." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

--- Post-incident follow-ups (planned):
- Add automated preflight check before driver/firmware rollouts: run nvme stress + small inference benchmark to validate no submission timeouts.
- Instrument NVMe controller reset count as an alert metric (threshold > 3 resets / 5m -> page).
- Add a runbook entry: if p99 spikes + nvme resets -> taint nodes -> route -> rollback driver -> contact vendor.
- Long-term: evaluate async NVMe flush strategies and isolation of inference disk activity from kernel-managed DMA paths.

danielle.p: action items assigned: me -> repro & staging test (ETA 2h). ingrid -> vendor ticket (ETA 1h). raj -> coordinate rollback plan (ETA 30m for canary). maria -> keep customer updated.

maria.g: I'll keep thread updated with logs and timeline. Starting to notify other customers that might be on same shard. :pray:
